A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REPVLM study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material and the renumbered SigLIP results.

before.justification: V1 reports original selective-classification experiments, ablations, OOD detection and qualitative data-curation results, including supplementary SigLIP evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional baseline comparisons and CLIP ViT-L/14 results.

M1.justification: The conditional Riemannian flow, training objective, density-based score and inference algorithms remain unchanged. Appendix B.2 changes eight residual blocks to six, matching the six already specified in v1 Table 5; this resolves inconsistent documentation without establishing an architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Conceptual Captions, DataComp and LAION proxies; the same six classification benchmarks; and ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-R and EuroSAT for OOD detection. Data-curation coverage is retained. Additional backbones change model configurations, not represented datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds Embedding Norm, W-CLIP, Conformity and Gaussian Mixture Model comparisons to the existing MCDO and ProbVLM comparisons in Table 2 and the SigLIP table. These substantially broaden evaluation to density and geometry alternatives. MC-Dropout is the renamed MCDO comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix B.6 adds CLIP ViT-L/14 evaluations within the retained zero-shot protocol. It also specifies SigLIP2-256, whereas v1 names SigLIP ViT-B/16; equivalence of those configurations is not established. Existing metrics, proxy sample counts, training budgets and ablation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The geometry/base-distribution, proxy-size and integration-step ablations retain their designs and results in Figure 3 and Tables 6–8. The dedicated OOD experiment and curation examples in Figures 4–5 are also retained. Expanded benchmark comparisons and explanatory discussion do not introduce a separate controlled analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use five different random seeds and report means with standard deviations. V2 extends the same reporting practice to additional comparisons; changed means and deviations do not establish a change in statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Many retained results change. For Conceptual Captions/CIFAR-100, Table 2 changes MCDO/REPVLM Acc@90 from 0.888/0.874 to 0.814/0.873, reversing their ordering. V2 adds four baseline result sets and CLIP ViT-L/14 results. The substantially revised SigLIP table includes negative REPVLM correlations on ImageNet-1K, but uncertain checkpoint equivalence prevents interpreting these as same-setting performance deterioration.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces claimed bidirectional relationships with an assumption-dependent chain. V2 explicitly rejects deriving pointwise Jacobian suppression from expectation-level optimality and removes the determinant/isometry density-preservation argument, treating proportional input and embedding densities as an empirical assumption. This substantially revises the central theoretical justification; Appendix A remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction recasts the theoretical contribution from a foundation to motivation, while Section 6 explicitly denies a formal identity and qualifies applicability by encoder geometry. The abstract and principal claims about the method, selective classification, OOD detection and curation remain largely unchanged; the conclusion still claims a rigorous link.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting comparator rankings to density-modeling quality and attributes SigLIP weaknesses to its training objectives and texture-sensitive representations. Sections 6 and B.6 substantially expand theoretical and applicability limitations. The impact statement develops the existing rarity/fairness warning into recommendations for subgroup evaluation and human review.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a reproduction-code URL, explicit backbone identifiers and a new classification-protocol subsection specifying prompts, normalized cosine-similarity prediction and the absence of a trained classification head. It also resolves the residual-block documentation inconsistency. These are useful disclosures; the principal training hyperparameters and hardware specification remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantive density-and-geometry research strand covering whitened CLIP, conformity, embedding norms and modality gaps. Additional references contextualize local linearization, the unresolved density-preservation argument and generative-model failure analogies. This broadens the paper's positioning beyond probabilistic embeddings and sampling-based uncertainty methods.

P1.justification: The central theoretical and main-results narratives are substantially rewritten: Section 3.1 adopts labeled A1–A3 links, and Section 5.2 is reorganized around the expanded comparisons. Limitations and impact prose are expanded, while Appendix B gains a classification-protocol subsection and a restructured backbone discussion.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is replotted with seven methods instead of three. Table 2 and the matched SigLIP table expand accordingly, and a new CLIP ViT-L/14 table is added. Figure 1 is revised and resized, while several retained figures and tables move. These substantially alter the central evidence displays.

improvement.justification: V1 overstates the theoretical density–uncertainty connection and mainly compares against dropout and ProbVLM. V2 distinguishes assumptions from derivation, adds directly relevant density/geometry baselines, and reports backbone-dependent weaknesses with an applicability discussion. These changes substantially improve scientific credibility, supported by clearer reproducibility information. The retained 'rigorous link' conclusion and inconsistent SigLIP naming remain defects, but do not outweigh these gains.
